text.p: Its sheer size would help Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co tide over the challenges that confront the Philippine banking industry, analysts predicting the bank's results said on Monday.

Lower loan growth triggered by a recent scare over asset quality, narrowing spreads, and keener competition have prompted many banking analysts to be conservative about prospects for Philippine banks.
But not for Metrobank, at least for this year.
A Reuter poll of six securities firms completed on Monday showed net income for the first six months of the year was expected to rise 32 percent to 2.68 billion pesos.
Full-year projections averaged 6.63 billion pesos, up 32.54 percent from 5.002 billion in 1996. The bank had earlier projected a 6.65 billion peso net income for this year.
"We expect strong growth for Metrobank, mainly due to its huge capital base," BNP Prime East analyst Marco Lucena said.
The bank had a net worth of more than 34 billion pesos as of end-May, the largest among more than 50 commercial banks operating in the country.
"In this industry, size really matters. That's the name of the game," Rachel Evangelista, an analyst at All AsiaCapital and Trust Corp, said.
Despite a marked slowdown in loan growth, areas like wholesale and trade financing in which Metrobank has a stronghold were doing well, Lucena said.

The industry's credit slowdown, which slumped to 34.7 percent in April from a high of 54.5 percent in September last year, has affected mostly consumer financing and real estate loans as banks became more prudent following troubles faced by banks in Thailand.
"In terms of loan growth, we believe Metrobank will outpace the industry. We still see a robust middle market," April Bautista, an analyst at DBS Securities, said.
She said spreads in trade financing remained profitable compared to the more competitive consumer and corporate loans market where there is fierce competition from domestic as well as foreign banks.
All Asia's Evangelista projected Metrobank's loans to rise by 34 percent this year.
Metrobank has grown on the strength of its Chinese-Filipino clientele, a niche market nurtured by its chairman George S.K. Ty, a leading member of the affluent community.
Mike Lecaros, analyst at Citisecurities, said loan growth would likely gain momentum in the second and third quarter this year as businesses start to build their inventories.
Metrobank reported a slight gain in its first quarter net to 1.25 billion pesos from one billion after it appropriated 500 million to provide for doubtful accounts.
Analysts believed that another huge provisioning was not likely in the rest of the year.
Despite the bullish short-term outlook, some analysts feared that constraints might surface in the coming years.
Angping Securities' Audi Pantillano said the industry as a whole might start consolidating as a result of the recent liberalisation of the industry.
"It's a natural development. It's a consequence of the efforts to liberalise the banking industry," he added.
